# When each region holds mallards (MODELED, eBird S&T v2025) — auto-generated by scripts/build_app.py

Weekly sum of relative abundance over each region's box. 'Jan / Oct' = Jan 1–19 average divided by October average:
above 1.2 = birds build into the late season (open water holds them); 0.6–1.2 = steady; below 0.6 = birds leave at freeze-up.
'Share' = region's part of all in-season mallards in Montana (boxes overlap a little at edges).

| Region | Season type | Oct | Nov | Dec | Jan 1–19 | Jan / Oct | Share | Fall peak week |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Hi-Line | Early season | 1255 | 916 | 442 | 230 | 0.18 | 11.2% | 10-25 |

| Billings–Yellowstone | Late season | 274 | 591 | 808 | 384 | 1.40 | 7.8% | 12-13 |
| SW Montana | All season | 331 | 492 | 450 | 310 | 0.94 | 6.2% | 11-29 |

Statewide: the year's biggest count is spring migration (week of 04-05); the fall/winter high is the week of 10-25. Fall builds in two steps: a late-October pulse of migrants, then a December build-up on open water.
